standard: NFPA 204 (2021 edition) - Table 9.2.4.2 Default Discharge Coefficients for Vents and Inlets, A.9.2.4.2, and Table A.8.2.6 Unit Heat Release Rates for Commodities
note: Transcribed from the printed pages 204-14 (Table 9.2.4.2), 204-23 (Table A.8.2.6) and 204-24 (A.9.2.4.2) of the 2021 edition. Table 9.2.4.2 gives the discharge coefficient to use for a vent or an inlet when the manufacturer provides none and the AHJ accepts no other value (9.2.4.2). A.9.2.4.2 is explanatory text, not a requirement: it calls 0.6 reasonable for most vents and for doors and windows that open at least 45 degrees, and says a louver can range from 0.1 to 0.4. Table A.8.2.6 is the heat release rate per unit floor area of the fully involved commodity, based on negligible radiative feedback from the surroundings and 100 percent combustion efficiency. It is for the stack height shown; A.8.2.6 says a rate for another height can be taken as proportional to height, based on the wood pallet rows. PE: polyethylene. PP: polypropylene. PS: polystyrene. PU: polyurethane. PVC: polyvinyl chloride. FRP: fiberglass-reinforced polyester.
